… And first grant that I may know how with inmost affection to mourn with those who sin; for this is a very great virtue, since it is written: “⟦And thou shalt not rejoice over⟧ the children of Judah in the day of their destruction, and speak not proudly in the day of their trouble.” Obad. 12.

Obadiah, so far as his writings are concerned, the briefest of all the prophets, speaks against Idumea, that is, the nation of Esau, that reprobate elder of the twin sons of Isaac and grandsons of Abraham. Now if, by that form of speech in which a part is put for the whole, we take Idumea as put for the nations, we may understand of Christ what he says among other things, “But upon Mount Sion shall be safety, and there shall be a Holy One.” ⟦Obad. 17⟧.
